Native sample review, 2026-10-19
All analysis was static or isolated CPU emulation with stubbed APIs.
No sample, dropped program, network connection, or installation was executed.

9da6438ad7bc7057cb8e39d7b9a77c0e6bde105377e49f6270cb07ccd52c65a4
MALICIOUS: Mirai-derived ARM IoT bot, statically linked with uClibc.
main (VA 0xd09c) unlinks argv[0], renames itself httpd, forks/setsid,
initializes attack and killer workers, and maintains its controller connection.
recv at 0xd7b0 feeds attack_parse at 0xd7c8 and attack_start at 0xd7fc.
The attack table includes TCP SYN/STOMP, GRE and UDP handlers. Raw packet
handlers use IP_HDRINCL and repeated sendto calls. This establishes DDoS
capability without relying on the attack-function names alone.
killer_exe reads /proc/PID/exe, compares whitelist/blacklist substrings and
sends SIGKILL at 0xcd5c. killer_maps has its own SIGKILL at 0xcef4.
Architecture-suffixed executable names occur in its whitelist, so they do not
prove payload delivery. Removed the delivery mapping from the rival-kill rule.
The SSDP template at file offset 0x1338c is selected through the payload table
at VA 0x1b654 by attack_method_nudp. That path creates SOCK_DGRAM sockets at
0xc554 and loops over send at 0xc698; it does not spoof the SSDP source.
The old amplification claim was replaced with a neutral template observation.
The old four-byte sendto-number signature first hit unaligned code at file
offset 0xae09. The real wrapper loads r7 at VA 0x13f2c, executes SVC at
0x13f30, and reads syscall 290 from 0x13f64. All five revised ARM rules bind
these instructions to the corresponding literal rather than any integer.
Independent parser, table-unlock and TCP/UDP symbol names identify the
unstripped Mirai variant. Individual names and kill logs remain neutral.

35458cc9189be3adfbd23255a0225b0e7dd8a1481687e107daa8dbc286f904ba
MALICIOUS: Floxif-infected Canon IJPLMSVC.exe 6.7.0.0.
The Canon identity and signing record describe the host, not a clean sample.
The image digest differs from its signed digest. EP VA 0x436317 jumps into
injected code at 0x430432, which walks the PEB loader list for GetProcAddress.
The 0x42e29a routine advances a saved return address by four bytes to skip
inline junk. The 0x42e2aa routine XORs and complements stack-built strings.
Isolated Unicorn emulation traced CreateFileA/ReadFile on the sample itself,
VirtualProtect of five bytes at the original EP, and restoration of those
bytes. It decoded an appended PE at file offset 0x708c4 and resolved FloodFix2
after LoadLibraryA. The decoded DLL was unpacked with UPX and exports
FloodFix/FloodFix2. Its file enumeration and PE-writing code corroborate the
parasitic payload. No filename family labels were treated as evidence.
A stack-byte run, PEB read and opaque overlay alone do not establish an
exploit or hostile shellcode loader. Replaced that hostile rule with a
suspicious obfuscation composite requiring the real return-skipping routine.
The Floxif identity and independent SigBase Floxif rule remain hostile.

f640e17c2f8491fc5b2676250da46cb15ec50250add3a6b5efb6daebec5f44bd
MALICIOUS: StormAttack installer/injector with a damaged embedded DLL.
CRT entry calls WinMain at VA 0x401cb0. The configuration word at 0x404120
selects mode 3, reaching 0x401900. That branch creates an Active Setup GUID
key, writes StubPath through RegSetValueExA at 0x401a4b, reads its own image,
patches and writes a copy, and passes the copied path to CreateProcessA.
It then calls the COMSPEC /c del cleanup function at 0x401390.
Other retained branches extract resource DLL/101, write a System32 DLL, and
replace LanmanServer's ServiceDLL value. The injection function at 0x401150
creates a target process, allocates/writes remote memory, resolves LoadLibraryA
and supplies that same resolved pointer as CreateRemoteThread's start address.
These are code capabilities, not claims that every installation branch runs.
Resource DLL/101 starts at file offset 0x5060, size 0x9c00. Its entry RVA
0x741a maps to offset 0x681a within the resource; the entry bytes are zero.
Its resource/relocation areas are also zeroed, and it lacks executable sections.
It retains StormAttack banners and protocol strings, but those do not prove
a functioning DNS, HTTP, download, ransomware or flood payload in this copy.
Retained the existing four hostile code-profile rules; added a neutral
zeroed-entry-region measurement for the damaged child. Successful injection
or persistence is not assumed.

Trait checks
build-fixtures.py creates 21 inert PE/ELF fixtures. check.py checks the exact
positive and near-miss IDs in cases.json through the full Cleave scanner.
The cases include integer-only syscall lookalikes, an incorrect literal-load
displacement, names in prose, a missing UDP identity leg, kill logging alone,
ordinary SSDP/architecture references, unchanged returns, and zero/unmapped PE
entry regions. No malware bytes are shipped in these fixtures.
The two moved handler-name atoms no longer promote the legacy attack-name
OR composites. Other consumers retain their existing attack evidence. The
new independent Mirai symbol cluster supplies identity coverage for this build.
The new YARA measurement maps AddressOfEntryPoint through section raw extents
without requiring executable flags, and requires all 32 bytes to be file-backed.
Its MZ string supplies evidence for the engine's inline-YARA result path.
